buylist.name: Breastfeeding chair
buylist.note: Sit in it before you buy, with your elbows where a feed would be. Second hand gliders go cheap and clean up fine.

buylist.name: Pram
buylist.note: Fold it and lift it in the shop before you commit, and check it actually fits your boot.

buylist.name: Capsule car seat
buylist.note: Must meet AS/NZS 1754 and be professionally fitted. Hiring one for the first year is normal and often cheaper.

buylist.name: Professional car seat fitting
buylist.note: Book a fitter before the due date. They come to you, and they will show you how to refit it yourself.

buylist.name: Bassinet
buylist.note: An adjustable head tilt helps reflux. The mattress must be firm, flat and the right size, with no gap at the edges.

buylist.name: Change table or chest of drawers
buylist.note: A low chest of drawers with a change mat on top does the same job, and still works long after the nappies stop.

buylist.name: Bassinet sheets
buylist.note: Three means one on, one in the wash, one for the 2am change. Fitted and snug, with no loose fabric.

buylist.name: Baby bouncer
buylist.note: Second hand is the norm here. For supervised awake time only, never for sleep (Red Nose).

buylist.name: Breastfeeding pillow
buylist.note: A firm one beats a squashy one. Handy for bottle feeds and for propping yourself up as well.

buylist.name: Baby bath
buylist.note: Top and tail washes cover the first week, so this can wait. Get one with a newborn insert you can take out.

buylist.name: Bath thermometer
buylist.note: 37 degrees is the number. Your elbow works, but this settles the argument.

buylist.name: Baby lounger
buylist.note: Supervised awake time only, never for sleep (Red Nose). Commonly passed on, so ask around before you buy.

buylist.name: Change mat
buylist.note: Wipe clean, with a raised edge. Two means one at the change table and one wherever you actually end up.

buylist.name: Baby hair brush
buylist.note: Soft bristles only. Gentle brushing helps lift cradle cap flakes.

buylist.name: Newborn nappies
buylist.note: Tooshies is a good brand. Do not stockpile one size, bub may skip newborn or grow out of it in a fortnight.

buylist.name: Milk storage bags
buylist.note: Freeze them lying flat so they stack. Date and label every single one.

buylist.name: Dimmable touch lamp
buylist.note: Dimmable and touch operated, so you can get light without properly waking anyone up.

buylist.name: Baby carrier
buylist.note: Try it on with weight in it. Look for a hip healthy design that holds their legs in an M shape.

buylist.name: Baby oil
buylist.note: Nice for baby massage. Newborn skin mostly needs nothing at all.

buylist.name: Electric nail filer
buylist.note: Far less frightening than scissors on tiny fingers. Easiest while they are fast asleep.

buylist.name: Nappy bin
buylist.note: A sealed bin saves the nursery. Check what the refill cartridges cost before you commit to the bin.

buylist.name: Nappy rash cream
buylist.note: Zinc based. Keep one at each change spot so you are never hunting for it one handed.

buylist.name: Baby towels
buylist.note: Hooded ones keep their head warm, which is the bit that matters coming out of the bath.

buylist.name: Rear view mirror for the car
buylist.note: Lets you see their face from the driver's seat. Fit it so it cannot come loose in a hard stop.

buylist.name: Sleep sacks
buylist.note: With arms for newborn to about 12 weeks, then sleeveless once they start rolling. Match the tog to the room.

buylist.name: Baby wipes
buylist.note: Buy the bulk box, you will get through it. Plain water wipes are kindest on brand new skin.

buylist.name: Face washers
buylist.note: Twenty is not too many. They end up as burp cloths, bibs and spill moppers anyway.

buylist.name: Burp cloths
buylist.note: Buy more than you think, then buy more again. This is the one thing nobody ever regrets over buying.

buylist.name: Onesies
buylist.note: Zips beat buttons at 3am. Get 0000 and 000, because newborn size does not last long.

buylist.name: Bodysuits and singlets
buylist.note: Envelope necks pull down over the body, which matters a lot when a nappy goes badly wrong.

buylist.name: Breast pump
buylist.note: Double electric if you plan to express often. Worth waiting until you know whether you need one.

buylist.name: Bottle warmer
buylist.note: A jug of warm water does the same job. Nice to have once night feeds settle into a pattern.

buylist.name: Bottle set
buylist.note: Start with a small set. Babies take against particular teats and brands, so do not commit to twelve of anything.

buylist.name: Bottle steriliser
buylist.note: Electric steam ones are quickest. Cold water sterilising tablets work fine and cost almost nothing.

buylist.name: Portable bottle warmer
buylist.note: Only earns its place if you are out a lot. An insulated flask of hot water is the cheap version.

buylist.name: Nipple cream
buylist.note: Lanolin based. Put it in the hospital bag, you will want it on day one and not on day three.

buylist.name: Disposable breast pads
buylist.note: Buy a box before the birth. Leaking starts when the milk comes in, around day three.

buylist.name: Washable breast pads
buylist.note: Kinder on the hip pocket once you know you need them. You will know by about week two.

buylist.name: Nipple shields
buylist.note: Only if you need them, and ideally after a chat with a lactation consultant or the ABA helpline.

buylist.name: Bottle teats in other flows
buylist.note: Teat flow is the usual culprit when a bottle feed goes badly. Keep a slower and a faster one on hand.

buylist.name: Spare steriliser basket
buylist.note: Saves waiting on a cycle at the worst possible moment. Only worth it if you are bottle feeding a lot.

buylist.name: Formula
buylist.note: A tin in the cupboard is insurance, not failure. Plenty of families end up combo feeding and all is well.

buylist.name: Bottle brush
buylist.note: A dedicated brush with a teat nub on the end. Replace it more often than feels necessary.

buylist.name: Bottle drying rack
buylist.note: Stops the bench disappearing under bottle parts. A clean tea towel works until it does not.

buylist.name: Cooler bag for expressed milk
buylist.note: For expressed milk in the car or the pram. Two ice bricks will see you through the trip home.

buylist.name: Maternity pads
buylist.note: The hospital gives you a few, not enough. Thick overnight ones, not regular pads. These are for Emma, not bub.

buylist.name: Peri bottle
buylist.note: Warm water while you wee makes the first week bearable. Ask the midwife to show you how.

buylist.name: Heat pack
buylist.note: For afterpains early on and for blocked ducts later. A microwavable wheat bag is plenty.

buylist.name: Going home clothes for Emma
buylist.note: Soft, loose, two sizes up from normal, nothing with a waistband. Dark colours, for obvious reasons.

buylist.name: Nursing bras
buylist.note: Wait until your milk settles, about week two, then buy the size you actually are. Three is the magic number.

buylist.name: One handed water bottle
buylist.note: Feeding makes you unbelievably thirsty and you will have one hand free. Flip top or straw, not a screw cap.

buylist.name: Dummies in three brands
buylist.note: Buy three different brands. Bub will reject two of them and you will never guess which two.

buylist.name: White noise machine
buylist.note: A phone app does the job for free. A separate machine means your phone stays in your pocket.

buylist.name: Portable nightlight
buylist.note: Rechargeable, one hand, warm light. Lives by the feeding chair and comes with you wherever you go.

buylist.name: Nappy caddy
buylist.note: A second change station for downstairs. By about week two you will be well and truly sick of the stairs.

buylist.name: Nappy transport bag
buylist.note: A sealed bag for dirty nappies in the pram or the car. Two means one is always clean and ready.

buylist.name: Pram rain cover
buylist.note: Melbourne. Get the one made for your pram, universal covers flap about and let the rain in.

buylist.name: Sun shade for the car window
buylist.note: Cling or roller type on the back windows. Afternoon sun straight onto a newborn is miserable for everyone.

buylist.name: Pram liner
buylist.note: It comes out and goes in the wash, which is the whole point. A folded muslin does a rough version.

buylist.name: Blackout blind
buylist.note: Melbourne summer mornings start early. A cheap stick on blind can buy you an extra hour of sleep.

buylist.name: Muslin wraps
buylist.note: Wrap, burp cloth, pram shade, mop. You will find a use for every one, so get more than six.

buylist.name: Thermometer for bub
buylist.note: Digital, for bub and not the bath. Know the number before you ring the nurse, it is the first thing they ask.

buylist.name: Feeding log
buylist.note: A cheap notebook beats any app at 3am. Jot down side, time and nappies for the first few weeks.

buylist.name: Laundry basics
buylist.note: Fragrance free sensitive detergent and a second basket. The washing load roughly triples overnight.

buylist.name: First aid basics
buylist.note: Infant paracetamol, saline drops, baby nail scissors, a few bandaids. Check doses with your pharmacist.

buylist.name: Hand me down clothes
buylist.note: Say yes to every bag offered. Newborn clothes are barely worn. Give them a wash before they go near bub.

buylist.name: The next size up
buylist.note: They grow out of 0000 in a few weeks. Have the next size in the drawer before the day you need it.

buylist.name: Cot
buylist.note: Around six months, when the bassinet gets tight. Check it meets AS/NZS 2172, and skip drop sides.

buylist.name: Cot mattress
buylist.note: Buy this one new. Firm, flat, and sized so you cannot fit two fingers between mattress and cot side.

buylist.name: Cot sheets
buylist.note: Fitted only, snug on the mattress. Three keeps you comfortably ahead of the washing.

buylist.name: Baby monitor
buylist.note: Audio only is plenty for most people. Video is for your peace of mind rather than for safety.

buylist.name: Sleeping bag, next size and tog
buylist.note: Around 3 to 6 months you need the next size and often a different tog. Sleeveless once they are rolling.

buylist.name: Travel cot
buylist.note: For holidays and nights at the grandparents. Nearly always borrowed. The mattress must be firm, flat and snug.

buylist.name: Convertible car seat
buylist.note: From about 12 months, AS/NZS 1754 and professionally fitted. Second hand needs its history and expiry known.

buylist.name: Play gym
buylist.note: From about 3 months. Almost always passed on, so ask around before you buy one new.

buylist.name: Teething toys
buylist.note: From about 4 months. Ones you can chill in the fridge, not freeze solid in the freezer.

buylist.name: Bibs
buylist.note: From about 6 months when solids start. The silicone catch all ones save the most washing.

buylist.name: High chair
buylist.note: From about 6 months. Check it meets AS 4684 and that the harness has five points.

buylist.name: Sippy cups
buylist.note: From about 6 months. A free flow or straw cup is better for their teeth than a hard spout.
